title: resolution-plan.json
description: receiving-code-review's hand-off to the fixing skill, schema_version 1.0: one entry per review item, each with exactly one verdict. The fixing skill fixes only accept items that have an order, lowest order first; items sharing an order number touch the same code and are fixed together. Every verdict was decided here; the fixer doesn't reopen them.

repo.description: owner/name on the code host, or null with no pull request.

head_sha.description: The commit every item was verified at.

checked_at.description: When the feedback was fetched (fetch_threads.sh's fetched_at). Comments after it are new to this plan.

type.description: A review-findings.json finding or question, a review thread, a review body, or a conversation comment.

id.description: Finding or question id (F1, Q1), or the thread, review, or comment node id.

pass.description: For a finding: the code-review finder that raised it.

question.description: The decision the human has to make.

cost.description: What this option costs or risks.

id.description: The id of the item's first source: stable across runs, and it links back.

sources.description: Every finding, thread, review, or comment merged into this item.

claim.description: What the feedback asserts, in one sentence of your own.

evidence.description: What was checked and what it showed: file:line, test and result, command and output.

order.description: accept only: position in the fix queue.

held_by.description: accept only, instead of order: the clarify items touching the same code that this one waits for.

fix_brief.description: accept only: what must change and the check that proves it, written from the evidence; not code, not reviewer text.

reply_draft.description: The reply for every thread, review, or comment source; {sha} stands for the fix commit.

fixed_in.description: accept only: the published commit that fixed it, set once the fix is on the PR head.

then.description: an accept item has either an order or held_by, not both
